title: Multiomics approaches reveal direct NF-kappaB p65 target genes in pancreatic islets during cytokine exposure and in type 1 diabetes.
authors: Martin, Thomas M; Burke, Susan J; Batdorf, Heidi M; Lipchik, Andrew M; Javvadi, Pravalika; Ghosh, Sujoy; Collier, J Jason
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学（RNA-Seq、ChIP-Seq）结合分子对接模拟，鉴定NF-κB p65在胰岛细胞中的直接靶基因，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点鉴定，但核心是疾病相关基因表达调控，互作机制建模深度有限。
abstract: Autoimmune diseases, including Type 1 diabetes (T1D), are often characterized by overactive inflammatory signaling pathways. The proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) elicits global gene expression changes in islet beta-cells which overlap with islets obtained from human donors with T1D. The direct transcriptional link between NF-kappaB subunit p65 and target genes involved with autoimmune events was investigated. We used a multiomics approach including bulk RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq), single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-Seq), and chromatin immunoprecipitation coupled to deep sequencing (ChIP-Seq), alongside molecular docking simulations, and transcriptional assays. Through the various experimental modalities, we identified early response genes driven by IL-1beta that were differentially expressed in pancreatic islets from human T1D donors and also conserved across mouse, rat, and human tissues. ChIP-Seq revealed genes that are direct genomic targets of the NF-kappaB p65 transcription factor. Moreover, regions that gained RNA polymerase II binding following cellular exposure to IL-1beta were identified, complementing the early response gene profile induced by beta-cell exposure to IL-1beta. Molecular docking simulations predicted that mutations reducing p65 transcriptional capacity do not alter DNA binding ability. These findings clearly show that IL-1beta signaling in pancreatic beta-cells directs p65 to specific genomic regions congruent with increased gene expression relevant to T1D in beta-cell lines as well as mouse and human islets exposed to cytokines. Islets from human donors with T1D express genes identified as direct p65 targets using unbiased approaches, implicating heightened NF-kappaB activity as a critical component of autoimmune disease etiology.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Using multiple Seq-based approaches, this study identified genes expressed in human pancreatic tissue from donors with Type 1 diabetes that are regulated acutely by exposure to the cytokine interleukin-1beta. The NF-kB transcription factor p65 (RelA) was determined via ChIP-Seq to be a major control node regulating this immediate early response. These collective datasets are consistent with a paradigm of overactive NF-kB signaling as a critical component of autoimmunity in both rodents and humans.
abstract_zh:
自身免疫性疾病，包括1型糖尿病（T1D），通常以过度活跃的炎症信号通路为特征。促炎细胞因子白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）在胰岛β细胞中引发全局基因表达变化，这些变化与来自人类T1D供体的胰岛重叠。本研究探讨了NF-κB亚基p65与涉及自身免疫事件的靶基因之间的直接转录联系。我们采用了多组学方法，包括批量RNA测序（RNA-Seq）、单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-Seq）和染色质免疫沉淀 coupled 深度测序（ChIP-Seq），并结合分子对接模拟和转录分析。通过多种实验模式，我们鉴定了由IL-1β驱动的早期反应基因，这些基因在人类T1D供体胰腺胰岛中差异表达，并在小鼠、大鼠和人类组织中保守。ChIP-Seq揭示了NF-κB p65转录因子的直接基因组靶基因。此外，我们识别了细胞暴露于IL-1β后获得RNA聚合酶II结合的区域，补充了β细胞暴露于IL-1β诱导的早期反应基因谱。分子对接模拟预测，降低p65转录能力的突变不改变DNA结合能力。这些发现明确表明，胰腺β细胞中的IL-1β信号传导将p65引导至特定基因组区域，与β细胞系以及暴露于细胞因子的小鼠和人类胰岛中与T1D相关的基因表达增加一致。来自人类T1D供体的胰岛表达通过无偏方法识别为直接p65靶标的基因，暗示增强的NF-κB活性是自身免疫性疾病病因的关键组成部分。

新意与贡献：本研究利用多种基于测序的方法，识别了来自1型糖尿病供体的人类胰腺组织中受细胞因子白细胞介素-1β急性调节的基因。通过ChIP-Seq确定NF-κB转录因子p65（RelA）是调控这种即时早期反应的主要控制节点。这些综合数据集与过度活跃的NF-κB信号传导作为啮齿动物和人类自身免疫关键组成部分的范式一致。
